title: A must-have
body:
I can't remember the last time I felt so strongly compelled to write a positive review.
I don't consider myself to have a problem with doom scrolling or screentime for the most part, but I have one digital vice - YouTube. I have premium and it's probably my favourite entertainment platform.
I noticed that my Screentime was creeping up over time into numbers that I wasn't comfortable with.
With all other apps I was wasting time with and knew they werent bringing me any value, I simply deleted them, cold turkey, about a year ago and have no regrets. But YouTube felt different, I do get genuine value from it whether that be entertainment, educational or practical. The problem was the volume and lack of intentionality.
Although it's early days I can whole heartedly say that one-sec has completely changed the dynamic and feels like the perfect solution I was missing all this time. In just one week my Screentime reduced by 45% while feeling like I wasn't even trying. Through a combination of blocking schedules and interventions, the frequency and duration I spend on YT has dropped dramatically and I can feel better habits forming already.
Often you really do only need the intervention, but I do like having the scheduled block features to stop me from checking work apps when I'm off the clock.
As others point out, the setup is a bit unconventional and less straightforward than some of the alternatives. But it is absolutely worth it, and the instructions are still clear enough.
More than happy to pay the modest annual fee for such a high-impact and well thought out experience.

title: My second time reviewing - milestone achieved
body:
This app has changed my life, and got me my most valuable asset back: 

My time.

Since May 2023, I have saved 4.3 weeks of SCREEN TIME on Instagram, and another couple weeks across multiple different social media’s.

Across the board, I have saved 1.4 MONTHS of screen time. Just think about that for onesec (excuse the pun) 

Overall ‘app opening’ preventions currently sit at 19,701. 

In fact, my milestone has now been achieved:

The blockers were genuinely so annoying to bypass, I started to get frustrated and it clearly conditioned my brain to resent the app in question that was being blocked, in this case, Instagram. I have now uninstalled Instagram, and I can say confidently that I am much happier without it. 

You actually realise after you don’t have some of these apps that their presence in your life is meaningless, and they literally give you zero value.

The only social media app I could justify using is “X”, which I still have yet to even use, but it’s a platform of free speech and uncensored content so that you can make your own informed decisions about the world without being reliant on mainstream media. Again, just make sure you have the blockers in place & re-interventions (stops you from doomscrolling / getting you into rabbit holes for hours) 

Nevertheless, it’s actually quite scary to think that some of us can’t live without social media. It used to be me. 

The truth is, whether or not you have social media on your phone, the world keeps spinning. It’s up to you to decide what you do with your time as it spins. 

I trust you’ll make the smart decision that I did back in May last year. Install the app and get your time back. 
 
Massive thank you to the developers, hopefully one day I’ll meet you and treat you all to a drink. 

Alex

title: Really really good
body:
This app is really really amazing and I’m glad it exists. It is already helping me to reduce certain compulsions to open certain apps, and prevents me from staying on each app too long.

There are some bugs or potential features though:

- “I don’t want to open this app” could pop out a bit earlier or maybe immediately so we can cancel right away. I know we can just navigate away from the app though but this would be a nice feature.
- PIP intentions don’t seem to show up for apps, only for Safari. Not sure why, am I doing something wrong or is this a known bug?
- video previews of the interventions (or an in-app simulation of the intervention)
- ensure that all interventions support features like Healthy alternatives. Eg I think that the circle tracing one doesn’t support this feature of Healthy alternatives. Along with this, some documentation such as a matrix of interventions and features, with checks/crosses, would be nice.
- morning countdown could work for other apps than just the delayed apps. Eg I don’t want to make it hard for me to use Telegram or WhatsApp but I may want to stop myself from using them in the morning when I wake up (I have friends in the East so they send me messages while I’m asleep so there is lots of temptation to reply to them when I wake up). But they shouldn’t be intervened any other time of the day.
